assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydrogen
items.clue: The gas made when a metal reacts with an acid; it burns with a squeaky pop.

items.label: Salt
items.clue: A compound, such as magnesium sulfate, made when an acid reacts with a metal.

items.label: Catalytic converter
items.clue: Part of a car exhaust where a precious metal speeds up changes to harmful gases

items.label: Indicator
items.clue: A substance that changes colour depending on how acidic or alkaline a solution is.

questions.stem: Which statement about a catalyst is correct?

options.text: It speeds up a reaction but is used up
It makes a reaction give more product
It speeds up a reaction and is not used up
It changes which products are made

questions.explanation: Yes. A catalyst makes a reaction go faster and is left over unchanged at the end, so it can be used again.

questions.stem: Manganese(IV) oxide speeds up the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. Afterwards, any solid left is filtered off and dried, with none spilled. How does its mass compare with the start?

options.text: It is the same as at the start
It is less, as some was used up
It is zero, as it became the oxygen
It is more, as it took in oxygen

questions.explanation: Yes. Manganese(IV) oxide is a catalyst: it speeds up the reaction but is not used up, so the same mass is recovered.

questions.stem: A car's catalytic converter contains the metal platinum, a catalyst. What does the platinum do?

options.text: Filters harmful gases out of the exhaust
Burns away as it reacts with harmful gases
Speeds up reactions that change harmful gases
Gives the engine extra energy from the fuel

questions.explanation: The catalyst speeds up reactions that turn harmful exhaust gases into less harmful ones.

questions.stem: A factory can speed up a reaction by heating it or by using a catalyst. Why might a catalyst be the better choice?

options.text: It speeds up the reaction without extra heating
It makes more product from the same reactants
It is a cheap reactant that gets used up
It heats the mixture using its own energy

questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up a reaction at a lower temperature, so less energy is needed for heating.

questions.stem: A reaction takes 60 s. With 1 g of powder X added it takes 10 s, and 1 g of X is recovered afterwards. What is X?

options.text: A reactant, as it was added at the start
A product, as it was there at the end
A fuel, as it gave the reaction energy
A catalyst, as it sped things up unchanged

questions.explanation: X made the reaction faster and its mass did not change, so it is a catalyst.

questions.stem: Manganese oxide speeds up the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. Why is it left out of the reactants in the equation?

options.text: Only a tiny amount of it is needed
It is not used up in the reaction
It is a solid, and reactants are liquids
It reacts too quickly to be recorded

questions.explanation: A catalyst is not used up or changed into a product, so it is not a reactant.
